sections.title: Executive Summary + Investment Thesis
sections.body:
**Executive Summary**
Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited has demonstrated a notable improvement in its financial performance for the year ended March 31, 2025. The company's profit for the year stood at ₹10,929 crore (109,290.4 million), representing a significant increase from ₹9,576 crore (95,763.8 million) in the previous year. This growth is reflected in the basic earnings per share, which rose to ₹45.6 from ₹39.9 in the previous year. The company's segment reporting highlights the diverse geographical presence, with revenues derived from the sale of pharmaceutical products across various regions, including India, the United States of America, emerging markets, and the rest of the world.

**Investment Thesis**
Our investment thesis for Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited is positive, driven by the company's improving profitability and diverse revenue streams. With a significant presence in multiple markets, the company is well-positioned to capitalize on growth opportunities in the pharmaceutical industry. The increase in profit for the year and earnings per share suggests a strong operational performance, which is expected to continue in the future. However, a detailed analysis of the company's financials, including revenue from operations and net worth, is required to further support this thesis. Unfortunately, the provided excerpts do not include this information, making it challenging to conduct a comprehensive peer comparison or derive specific ratios and percentages. Nonetheless, based on the available data, we believe that Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited presents an attractive investment opportunity, driven by its robust financial performance and diversified business model.

sections.title: Business Overview + Segment Breakdown
sections.body: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited operates in the pharmaceutical industry, with a diverse business mix across geographies. As of FY25, the company's revenue share is broken down into US Business (31%), India Business (33%), Emerging Markets (18%), Rest of the World (RoW) (14%), and API and Others (4%). The company leads the pharmaceutical market in India in value and prescription volumes, with India Formulation sales reaching ₹169 billion [Consolidated] in FY25, accounting for approximately 33% of overall revenues. The company's growth in India is driven by higher volumes and new product launches. In the US, revenue grew by 5.8% to ₹162 billion [Consolidated], driven by Specialty sales. The company's sales in Emerging Markets grew by 9.2% to ₹94 billion [Consolidated], while sales in RoW markets grew by 6.7% to ₹72 billion [Consolidated]. The Global Specialty revenue recorded a strong 17.1% growth to reach ₹9.72 billion [Consolidated] (assuming 1 USD = 80 INR, actual conversion not provided) during FY25.

sections.title: Financial Performance
sections.body: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited reported a robust financial performance in FY25, with consolidated revenue growth of 9.0% over FY24, driven by its India and Emerging Markets business, which recorded a 13.7% and 9.2% year-on-year increase, respectively. The company's US business reported a 5.8% rise in revenue, while Rest of the World markets registered steady growth compared to the previous year. Consolidated EBITDA grew by 17.3%, with an EBITDA margin of 29%, reflecting improved operating leverage. Adjusted net profit rose by 19% year-on-year, underscoring the company's commitment to profitable growth. The consolidated net profit [Consolidated] for FY25 was ₹109,801.0 million, while the consolidated revenue [Consolidated] was ₹525,784.4 million. The company's net worth [Consolidated] increased by 13.4% to ₹722 billion in FY25 from ₹637 billion in FY24.

sections.title: Balance Sheet Health + Cash Flow
sections.body:
The balance sheet health of Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited appears to be stable, with no material uncertainty existing as on the date of the audit report that the company is not capable of meeting its liabilities existing at the date of balance sheet as and when they fall due within a period of one year from the balance sheet date. In terms of cash flow, the filing excerpts do not provide explicit information on the company's cash flow position. However, the fact that the company's auditors have stated that they have no reason to believe that the company will not be able to meet its liabilities as they fall due within the next year suggests that the company's cash flow position is likely to be stable. sections.title: Key Risks
sections.body:
The 'Key Risks' section of this report highlights potential challenges that Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Limited may face. One key risk is related to the company's financial assets, which are measured at fair value with all changes recognised in the statement of profit and loss. This may lead to volatility in the company's profit and loss statement, particularly if there are significant changes in the fair value of these assets. Additionally, the company's derecognition policy for financial assets may also pose a risk, as it may lead to a delay in the recognition of losses or gains on the sale of investments.

Another key risk is the company's dependence on its reportable segments, which derive their revenues from the sale of pharmaceutical products. The company's performance is evaluated by the Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM) based on an analysis of various performance indicators by these segments. Any decline in the performance of these segments, particularly in the India, United States of America, Emerging markets, and Rest of the world segments, may have a significant impact on the company's overall revenue and profitability. However, specific financial metrics and potential risks associated with these segments are not provided in the given excerpts, making it challenging to assess the magnitude of these risks.

When it has neither transferred nor retained substantially all of the risks and rewards of the asset, nor transferred control of the asset, the Company continues to recognise the transferred asset to the extent of the Company’s continuing involvement. The transferred asset and the associated liability are measured on a basis that reflects the rights and obligations that the Company has retained.
